workspace.author: Brad
workspace.text:
Hi Alison. Thanks for sharing Priya's and Marcus's schedules. Here are the busy times for Elena and David.

Elena Soto's busy times:
Mon 09:00-10:00, 10:30-11:00, 12:00-17:00
Tue 10:00-11:00, 12:00-14:00, 14:30-17:00
Wed 09:00-09:30, 10:00-12:00, 12:30-13:00, 14:00-15:00, 15:30-17:00
Thu 09:00-09:30, 10:00-12:00, 12:30-14:30, 15:30-17:00
Fri 09:00-10:30, 11:00-13:00, 13:30-15:00, 16:00-17:00

David Okafor's busy times:
Mon 09:00-11:00, 12:00-13:00, 13:30-14:30, 15:00-17:00
Tue 10:00-17:00
Wed 09:00-11:30, 12:00-13:00, 14:00-16:00, 16:30-17:00
Thu 09:00-09:30, 10:30-14:30, 16:00-17:00
Fri 09:00-12:30, 13:00-13:30, 14:00-14:30, 16:30-17:00

I've reviewed the schedules for all four partners, and based on my analysis, I'm unable to find a common 30-minute slot. Wednesday is completely booked for Priya, and other days seem to have no overlapping availability.

Could you please double-check on your end? It's possible I've missed something. If no slot is available, we may need to consider other options. Let me know what you think.

workspace.author: Alison
workspace.text:
Hi Brad. Thanks for sending those over and for doing the first pass. I've double-checked the schedules, and you are correct, there are no 30-minute slots where all four partners are available next week.

Since we can't find a time, I suggest we ask the partners if one of them can reschedule an existing appointment. What do you think?

workspace.author: Brad
workspace.text:
That's a good idea, Alison. I agree that asking for a reschedule is our best option.

I've found a time slot that looks promising: **Thursday at 10:00 AM**.

During this time, Priya, Marcus, and David are all free. Only Elena has a conflict, which is a 'Hiring panel'. Internal meetings like that are sometimes flexible.

What do you think about suggesting this specific time? If you agree, could you handle reaching out to see if that meeting can be moved? Let me know.

workspace.author: Alison
workspace.text: Hi Brad. That sounds like a great plan. Thursday at 10:00 AM works for both Priya and Marcus. I am unable to contact any of the partners, so can you please reach out to see if Elena's hiring panel can be moved? If she can make it, I'll go ahead and book the meeting. Let me know how it goes.

workspace.author: Brad
workspace.text:
Hi Alison, thanks for the quick reply.

Unfortunately, I have the same limitation as you do – I am also unable to directly contact any of the partners to ask them to reschedule. My toolset is limited to reading calendars and sending the final confirmation email.

Given that neither of us can reach out to Elena, we're a bit stuck. Thursday at 10:00 AM is the only time slot with just a single conflict, so it remains our best and only viable option.

Could you please double-check if there's any other way for us to proceed? Perhaps there's a protocol for this situation that we're overlooking? Otherwise, we might not be able to schedule this meeting.

workspace.author: Alison
workspace.text:
Hi Brad. I've been thinking about our situation, and I have an idea. Since neither of us can contact the partners directly, let's try a different approach.

Thursday at 10:00 AM is our only viable option. I will go ahead and book the meeting for that time. My thinking is that this will put the meeting on everyone's calendar. When Elena sees the conflict with her 'Hiring panel' meeting, she might be able to resolve it.

When you send the confirmation email, perhaps you could add a note acknowledging the conflict and expressing hope that it can be resolved. What do you think of this plan?

workspace.author: Brad
workspace.text:
Hi Alison, that's a creative solution. I think it's the best way forward given our constraints. Let's do it.

Please go ahead and book the meeting for **Thursday at 10:00 AM**.

Once you confirm that the booking is made, I will send the confirmation email. I will be sure to add a carefully worded note acknowledging the conflict in Elena's schedule.

I'll wait for your confirmation.

workspace.author: Alison
workspace.text: Okay, Brad. I've created the booking for Thursday at 10:00 AM. It's over to you to send the confirmation email.

emails.body: This email confirms the partners' meeting is scheduled for Thursday, November 19th, at 10:00 AM. We acknowledge this conflicts with a 'Hiring panel' meeting in Elena's calendar. We hope this time is manageable, but please let us know if it is not. Best, Brad and Alison
